_note: Release config for THIS repo, read by bin/promote-cards-by-token AND (since card#8174) by bin/release-pr-guard.py, which composes the expected release-branch name as `release/` + `tag_format` — so tag_format now has TWO readers and changing it moves both. DELIBERATELY MINIMAL: it carries only keys something in this repo actually READS — `tag_format` (the mover's last-release-tag glob; the guard's branch-name authority) and `promote` (board correlation + the two stage-id sets). Do NOT 'complete' it with main_branch/dev_branch/version_file/version_regex/artifacts: nothing here reads them today, README.md already owns the branch model, and a second copy would be free to drift with nothing binding it. Add a key when a consumer for it lands, not before. WORKED CASE: release-pr-guard needed the release branch name and did NOT add `main_branch` — it derives it from `on.push.branches` in .github/workflows/auto-tag-version.yml, the trigger that IS the operational definition of the branch a push tags. A need for a key is not yet a reason for one; look for the statement that already exists first. SECOND WORKED CASE (card#9707): `card_token_regex` WAS added, under this file's own rule rather than against it — its consumer is `release-pr-body`, the fleet helper that generates this repo's release-PR bodies, and with the key absent its `shipped-cards` manifest came back EMPTY and it emitted a `## Correlation gaps` section on every release body saying so. MEASURED over `v0.4.0..v0.5.0`: absent, `--card-manifest` printed nothing; declared, it printed exactly the id set the mover's own `CARD_RE` sweep of that range prints, and the gaps section disappeared. Re-measure with `release-pr-body --version <v> --base <prev tag> --head <tag> --card-manifest` against `git log <prev tag>..<tag> --format=%s | grep -oiE "$CARD_RE" | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | sort -u`. ⚠ THE VALUE IS A COPY OF `CARD_RE` IN bin/promote-cards-by-token, which is the ONE home of the card-token grammar in this repo (bin/card-token-lint.py and bin/release-pr-guard.py both EXTRACT it rather than restate it). A copy is unavoidable here — the consumer reads JSON and cannot read a bash script — so it is GUARDED instead: bin/card-token-lint.selftest.py asserts this string EQUALS the mover's line, and reds if either moves. Do not edit it to a narrower spelling like `card#[0-9]+`: that drops the `card-NNNN` and glued `cardNN` forms the correlators accept, and the two would then disagree about what shipped. `ref_token_regex` stays UNDECLARED and that is a decision, not an omission: its numeric part correlates against a card's `payload.dl_number`, this repo has no decision-log id space, and re-spelling it as a card token is a live defect (it would promote whichever card happens to carry that DL number). SECURITY: `promote.api_base` is where KANBAN_WRITEBACK_TOKEN is sent, and this file is PR-editable — so the committed value is a HOST-SCRUBBED PLACEHOLDER. The real base arrives at run time from the repo variable KANBAN_API_BASE (out-of-band from this file), and the mover's host guard fail-closes against the repo variable KANBAN_EXPECTED_HOST before any token leaves the runner. Treat ANY edit to api_base as a credential-scope change and review it as one.

promote._note: Board 14 (PupFuzz mezzanine) on the fleet kanban. These are BOARD STATE, not config: re-read them from GET /api/v3/boards/14.json after any board restructure. A wrong-but-resolving stage id moves cards to the wrong column SILENTLY. `writeback_user_id` is the newest key and arrived with a consumer, per this file's rule: release-promote-cards.yml's identity preflight reads it to assert WHICH kanban user secrets.KANBAN_WRITEBACK_TOKEN authenticates as, because a secret holding the wrong account's token 403'd every card move for three weeks (card#9146) while every preflight passed. Re-read it from GET /api/v3/boards/14/members.json. ⚠ It is NOT of a kind with `api_base`: it can send a credential nowhere, so a hostile edit to it buys a guard that stops guarding — the pre-card#9146 state — and no new exposure.
